title: Behold the Saviour on the Cross
description: Behold the Saviour on the Cross in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 231 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Crucifixion of Christ”, where the book credits them to the Christian Psalmist.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold the Sa-viour on the cross, A spec-ta-cle of woe! See from his ag-o-niz-ing wounds The blood in-ces-sant flow;

lines: Behold the Saviour on the cross,
Till death's pale ensigns o'er his cheek
Till light forsook his closing eyes,
For sins, but not his own;
All old things now are past away,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
